title: Cantar de mio Cid
titleEn: The Song of the Cid — The Cid dresses for the court and enters it (tirada 137, lines 3060–3126)
part: Tirada 137 (first part) · The Cid dresses for the court and enters it (lines 3060–3126)
source: Ramón Menéndez Pidal (ed.), Poema de mio Cid, 2.ª edición corregida (Clásicos Castellanos 24; Madrid: Ediciones de “La Lectura”, 1923), pp. 317–321, lines 3060–3126 (tiradas 137–137). Text follows Pidal's critical text exactly, including its old accentuation and mixed spellings; Pidal's italics (his editorial restorations) are shown in [brackets], and a line he restores whole is flagged in its note. Line numbers are Pidal's. Pronunciation convention: reconstructed twelfth-century Castilian. Translations made fresh from the Old Spanish; Pidal's notes and vocabulary (1908–11) the lexical aids.

sentences.t:
Matines e prima dixieron faza l[os] albor[es],
suelta f[o] la missa antes que saliesse el sol,
e ssu ofrenda han fecha muy buena e [a sazón].
sentences.l:
Matins and prime they-said towards the dawns,
finished was the mass before that should-rise the sun,
and their offering they-have made very good and [in season].
sentences.i: They sang matins and prime towards the dawn; the mass was over before the sun rose, and they made their offering, a rich one and duly given.
sentences.n: Tirada 137 (assonance ó) — the Çid makes ready at San Servando and goes in to the court at Toledo; the king offers him a seat on his own bench, and the Çid declines (Pidal: Preparación del Cid en San Servando para ir a la corte.—El Cid va a Toledo y entra en la corte. El rey le ofrece asiento en su escaño. El Cid rehusa). The line-ends run albor[es], sol, [a sazón], mejor, Jero[me], Gustioz … Carrión: stressed ó, a new assonance and a new tirada. The tirada runs on well past v. 3126 (the king opens the session, and the Çid makes his demands); it continues in the next part. Matines e prima, 'matins and prime', the night office and the first hour of the day, sung in the church of San Servando where the Çid kept his vigil (end of the last part). dixieron, 'they said' (decir of the hours of the office). faza l[os] albor[es], 'towards the dawn' (faza = hacia, f- for h-); the os of los and the es of albores are in Pidal's italic, his restorations. suelta f[o] la missa, 'the mass was finished' (suelta, 'loosed, ended', literally 'released', our reading of the participle; f[o] = fue, the o Pidal's). antes que saliesse el sol, 'before the sun rose' (imperfect subjunctive after antes que, as now). e ssu ofrenda, 'and their offering' (ssu = su: the s is doubled after e, a spelling of the join between words). han fecha, 'they have made', the participle agreeing with ofrenda, as old Spanish often does; fecha = hecha, f- for h-. muy buena e [a sazón], 'very good and in season, timely': the whole of a sazón is in Pidal's italic, his restoration (he gives no footnote; a sazón, 'at the right time, fittingly', is our reading of the phrase).

sentences.t:
“Vos Minaya Álbar Fáñez, el mio braço mejor.
vos iredes comigo e obispo don Jero[me]
e Per Vermu[doz] e aqueste Muño Gustioz
e Martín Antolínez, el Burgalés de pro,
sentences.l:
“You Minaya Álbar Fáñez, the my arm best.
you you-will-go with-me and bishop don Jero[me]
and Per Vermu[doz] and this Muño Gustioz
and Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese of worth,
sentences.i: “You, Minaya Álvar Fáñez, my best right arm, you shall go with me, and the bishop Don Jerome, and Per Vermudoz, and Muño Gustioz here, and Martín Antolínez, the worthy man of Burgos,
sentences.n: The Çid names the men who will ride with him into the court; his speech runs to v. 3081. The speaker is not named: the poem goes straight from the mass to his words. Vos Minaya Álbar Fáñez, 'you, Minaya Álvar Fáñez' (house; Álbar kept in the literal line). el mio braço mejor, 'my best arm', article + possessive (el mio). Pidal ends v. 3063 with a full stop and begins v. 3064 with small vos, as printed: the sentence runs on, and the stop is kept. iredes = iréis, 'you will go' (future of ir, old -edes ending). comigo = conmigo. e obispo don Jero[me], 'and the bishop Don Jerome' (house), the me Pidal's; obispo without the article. Per Vermu[doz], the doz Pidal's: 'Per Vermudoz' (house). aqueste = este, 'this': aqueste Muño Gustioz, 'Muño Gustioz here', the messenger who has just come back from the king (house: Muño Gustioz). el Burgalés de pro, 'the man of Burgos, of worth' (de pro, 'of worth, worthy'; pro, 'profit, worth').

sentences.i: and Álvar Álvarez and Álvar Salvadórez, and Martín Muñoz, born at a lucky moment, and my nephew Félez Muñoz;
sentences.n: Álbar Albar[oz], 'Álvar Álvarez' (house), the oz Pidal's; Álbar Salvadórez, 'Álvar Salvadórez'. que en buen punto nació, 'who was born at a good moment': punto, 'moment, point of time', in the place of the ora of the formula that belongs to the Çid (en buen ora naçió); here it is said of another knight. nació without the cedilla here, as printed (naçió elsewhere in this part). mio sobrino Félez Muñoz, 'my nephew Félez Muñoz' (house), who found the Çid's daughters at Corpes. The verse is short; Pidal prints it so.

sentences.i: with me shall go Mal Anda, who is well versed in the law, and Galín García, the good knight of Aragon; with these let a hundred be made up of the good men who are here.
sentences.n: irá, 'will go' (future of ir). Mal Anda, a name, left as it stands (it means 'goes badly'). Pidal's note to v. 3070: 'Mal Anda debió ser personaje real, al menos un "molino de Mal Anda" se menciona en una escritura de 1140, en Villahizán de Treviño, al Norte de Burgos. Era Mal Anda uno de los muchos sabidores que concurrían a la corte, según el v. 3005' — 'Mal Anda must have been a real person; at least a "mill of Mal Anda" is mentioned in a deed of 1140, at Villahizán de Treviño, north of Burgos. Mal Anda was one of the many sabidores who came to the court, according to v. 3005.' sabidor, 'learned, knowing': at v. 3005 the sabidores were men learned in the law (last part), and that is the sense here. Galind Garçiez, 'Galín García' (house; the manuscript form kept in the literal line). el bueno d' Aragón, 'the good one of Aragon', with d' for de before a vowel, as printed. con estos cúnplansse çiento, 'with these let a hundred be made up' (cúnplansse = cúmplanse, present subjunctive of command, cumplir 'to fill up, complete', with se: the -ss- as printed). de los buenos que i son, 'of the good men who are here' (i = allí, 'there, here').

sentences.t:
Velmezes vestidos por sufrir las guarnizones,
de suso las lorigas tan blancas commo el sol;
sentences.l:
Quilted-tunics put-on for to-bear the armour,
above the hauberks so white as the sun;
sentences.i: Let padded tunics be put on to bear the weight of the armour, and over them the hauberks, as bright as the sun;
sentences.n: The Çid gives the order of dress, in phrases without a main verb: 'quilted tunics put on … above them the hauberks …', each a short absolute clause, the way an order is given. Velmezes, plural of velmez, a padded or quilted garment worn under the mail (so understood here from the line itself: por sufrir las guarnizones, 'to bear the armour'). Pidal's note to v. 3073: 'Velmezes, v. p. 105' — 'Velmezes, see p. 105' (a page of his introduction: the poem begins on p. 123, so this is not part of the text). vestidos, 'put on, worn' (participle). sufrir, 'to bear, withstand'. guarnizones, 'armour, harness'. de suso, 'above, on top'. lorigas, 'hauberks, coats of mail'. tan blancas commo el sol, 'as white as the sun', bright polished steel (commo = como).

sentences.i: over the hauberks, ermines and fur robes, the cords tied fast so that no armour shows; under the mantles the swords, fine-tempered and keen;
sentences.n: armiños e pelliçones, 'ermines and fur robes' (pelliçones, house 'fur-robes'): the mail is worn hidden under court dress. e que no parescan las armas, 'and so that the arms may not show' (que + subjunctive of purpose; parescan = parezcan, from pareçer 'to appear'). bien presos los cordones, 'the cords well tied' (presos, participle of prender 'to take, fasten'), another phrase without a verb. so = bajo, 'under'. dulçes e tajadores, 'smooth and cutting': dulçe, literally 'sweet', said of a blade, is taken here as 'fine, well-tempered' (the sense is not glossed by Pidal here; our reading). tajadores, -dor adjective, one form for both genders, here with fem. espadas (house: 'cutting').

sentences.t:
d' aquesta guisa quiero ir a la cort,
por demandar mios derechos e dezir mi[e] razón.
sentences.l:
of this manner I-want to-go to the court,
for to-claim my rights and to-say my case.
sentences.i: in this array I mean to go to the court, to claim my rights and to state my case.
sentences.n: d' aquesta guisa, 'in this manner' (aquesta = esta; guisa, 'manner, fashion'). cort, 'court' (house), the royal assembly at Toledo. por demandar, 'in order to claim' (por + infinitive of purpose). mios derechos, 'my rights'. dezir mi[e] razón, 'to say my say, state my case' (razón, 'speech, matter'): mie is the old feminine form of the possessive (mi), its e in Pidal's italic, restored by him.

sentences.t:
Si desobra buscaren ifantes de Carrión,
do tales çiento tovier, bien seré sin pavor.”
sentences.l:
If outrage they-should-seek infantes of Carrión,
where such hundred I-may-have, well I-shall-be without fear.”
sentences.i: If the Infantes of Carrión should go looking for trouble, where I have a hundred such as these I shall be quite without fear.”
sentences.n: desobra, an unknown word: Pidal's note to v. 3080: 'desobra, voz desconocida que parece "demasía, desmán"' — 'desobra, an unknown word that seems to mean "excess, outrage"'. The rendering follows him, and is to that degree uncertain. buscaren, 'they should seek', future subjunctive in the if-clause. ifantes de Carrión without the article, as often. do = donde, 'where'. tales çiento, 'a hundred such'. tovier = tuviere, 'I should have', future subjunctive of tener with its final -e dropped (apocope). bien seré sin pavor, 'I shall be well without fear' (bien, intensifying). The Çid's speech ends here.

sentences.t:
Respondieron todos: “nos esso queremos, señor.”
Assí commo lo ha dicho, todos adobados son.
sentences.l:
Answered all: “we that want, lord.”
Just as it he-has said, all equipped are.
sentences.i: They all answered: “That is our wish, my lord.” Just as he had said, they all made ready.
sentences.n: nos esso queremos, 'we want that' (nos = nosotros; esso = eso). Assí commo lo ha dicho, 'just as he has said it'. todos adobados son, 'all are equipped' (adobar, 'to equip, make ready'): the present with ha dicho, the perfect, where English keeps to the past, epic tense-mixing.

sentences.t:
Nos detiene por nada el que en buen ora naçió:
calças de buen paño en sus camas metió,
sobrellas unos çapatos que a grant huebra son.
sentences.l:
Not-himself delays for nothing he who in good hour was-born:
hose of good cloth on his legs he-put,
over-them some shoes that with great work are.
sentences.i: He who was born in a good hour does not linger for anything: he drew hose of fine cloth on his legs, and over them shoes richly worked.
sentences.n: Pidal indents v. 3084, a fresh paragraph: now the Çid's own dress, piece by piece. Nos detiene = non se detiene, 'he does not stop, does not delay' (Nos before a verb = non + se, house). por nada, 'for anything'. el que en buen ora naçió, 'he who was born in a good hour', the en buen ora formula (house, in its 'born' form). calças, 'hose, leggings'. Pidal's note to v. 3085: 'camas, "piernas"' — 'camas, "legs"'. metió, 'he put'. sobrellas = sobre ellas, 'over them'. çapatos, 'shoes'. Pidal's note to v. 3086: 'a grant huebra, "con muchas labores o adornos"; comp. 2401' — 'a grant huebra, "with much work or ornament"; compare v. 2401' (huebra, 'work', from Latin opera). The present son beside the preterite metió, as printed.

sentences.i: He put on a shirt of linen as white as the sun, with all its fastenings of gold and silver, close-fitting at the wrist, for so he had ordered it;
sentences.n: Vistió camisa, 'he put on a shirt' (no article). Pidal's note to v. 3087: 'rançal, "tela de hilo", v. 183' — 'rançal, "linen cloth", see v. 183' (the print has a stray second quote mark after the comma, 'tela de hilo',' v. 183, left out here). Pidal's note to v. 3088: 'presa, "presilla" (?)' — 'presa, "loop, fastening" (?)': his question mark, so the sense is not sure; we follow him. con oro e con plata todas las presas son, 'all the fastenings are with gold and with silver', made of or worked in them. al puño bien están, 'they sit well at the wrist' (puño, 'wrist, cuff'). Pidal's note to v. 3089: 'ca él se lo mandó (?); "car il l'a ainsi voulu", D. Hinard; "denn er hatte es [so] befohlen", Adam' — 'ca él se lo mandó (?); "for he willed it so", D. Hinard; "for he had ordered it [so]", Adam' (the square brackets are Adam's, as Pidal prints them). Pidal marks the half-line with a question mark and gives no reading of his own; ca, 'for', and se lo mandó, 'he had ordered it so', is how we take it, after Adam: se is the dative before lo (= le, old gelo), 'to them', the persons he gave the order to (the makers, presumably) left unsaid; the reading is uncertain, as Pidal flags it.

sentences.t:
sobrella un brial primo de çiclatón,
obrado es con oro, pareçen por o son.
sentences.l:
over-it a tunic fine of ciclaton,
worked it-is with gold, they-shine where they are.
sentences.i: over it a fine tunic of silk brocade, worked with gold, its ornament gleaming wherever it lay.
sentences.n: sobrella = sobre ella, 'over it' (the camisa). brial, 'tunic' (house: briales 'tunics'). primo, 'fine, choice'. çiclatón, 'ciclaton' (house), a rich silk: Pidal's note to v. 3090: '"un brial (p. 109) primoroso de seda" o, mejor dicho, de "brocado", como se ve por el verso siguiente' — '"a tunic (p. 109) finely made of silk" or, better, of "brocade", as the next line shows'. Pidal's note to v. 3091: '"labrado es con oro, las [labores o huebras] relumbran por donde están", según interpreta Bello. Para el sustantivo huebras, embebido en el verbo obrado, comp. 511. Generalmente el ciclatón iba tejido con oro' — '"it is worked with gold; the [work or ornaments] gleam wherever they are", as Bello interprets it. For the noun huebras, implied in the verb obrado, compare v. 511. The ciclaton was generally woven with gold' (the square brackets Pidal's). So pareçen, 'they appear, shine out', has huebras, the 'works' understood from obrado, as its subject. o = do, 'where' (as at v. 102, house); por o son, 'wherever they are'. obrado es, 'it is worked'.

sentences.t:
Sobresto una piel vermeja, las bandas d' oro son,
siempre la viste mio Çid el Campeador.
sentences.l:
Over-this a skin red, the bands of gold are,
always it wears my Çid the Campeador.
sentences.i: Over this a red fur, its bands of gold — my Çid the Campeador wears it always.
sentences.n: Sobresto = sobre esto, 'over this'. una piel vermeja, 'a red fur, a red fur-lined robe' (piel, 'skin, fur', the garment; vermeja = bermeja, 'red'). Pidal's note to v. 3092: 'banda significa "ceñidor"; pero más natural sería entender "franja". Los pellizuelos llevaban franjas en el cuello, en las bocamangas y en el borde de la falda' — 'banda means "girdle"; but it would be more natural to take it as "band, border". The little fur robes had borders at the neck, at the cuffs and at the hem of the skirt.' The rendering follows his more natural reading, 'bands, borders'. las bandas d' oro son, 'the bands are of gold'. siempre la viste, 'he always wears it' (viste, present of vestir): the narrator's aside, as if the robe were a known one.

sentences.i: A coif of fine linen over his hair, worked with gold and made for a purpose: that none should pull the good Çid Campeador by the hair;
sentences.n: cofia, 'coif', a close cap of cloth. sobre los pelos, 'over the hair' (pelos, 'hairs, hair'). Pidal's note to v. 3094: 'escarín (en los otros textos que me son conocidos "escari"), tela muy fina de hilo' — 'escarín (in the other texts known to me "escari"), a very fine linen cloth'. de pro, 'of worth, fine'. Pidal's mark after pro is damaged on the scan (a dot with something below it); it is read as a comma, which the sense (the line runs on) supports. con oro es obrada, 'it is worked with gold'. fecha por razón, 'made for a reason, with a purpose' (our reading: the purpose follows, que …). Pidal's note to v. 3096: 'Al vestirse tiene el Cid especial cuidado en proteger los cabellos; pone la cofia para recogerlos y que no puedan arrancárselos (esto debe significar contalassen, verbo desconocido), y además sujeta la barba, como dice el verso siguiente' — 'In dressing, the Cid takes special care to protect his hair; he puts on the coif to gather it up so that they cannot pull it out (this must be what contalassen means, an unknown verb), and he also ties up his beard, as the next line says.' So contalassen, 'they might pull', imperfect subjunctive of purpose, is Pidal's guess at an unknown verb. nol = non le, 'not … him', the le cut to l and glued on; al buen Çid Campeador repeats the him: they might not pull the hair of the good Çid.

sentences.t:
la barba avie luenga e prísola con el cordón,
por tal lo faze esto que recabdar quiere todo lo s[o].
sentences.l:
the beard he-had long and he-bound-it with the cord,
for such it he-does this that to-secure he-wants all the his.
sentences.i: his beard he wore long, and he bound it with the cord; this he does because he means to secure all that is his.
sentences.n: la barba avie luenga, 'the beard he had long' (avie = avié, 'he had', aver; luenga = larga, 'long'; avie unaccented here, as printed, avié at v. 3124). prísola = priso + la: priso, the old strong preterite of prender, 'he took, fastened', + la, 'it', glued on. el cordón, 'the cord'. Pidal's note to v. 3097: 'El mesar la barba era una de las más graves injurias (p. 119, n.), y temiendo el Cid un insulto, recoge la barba con un cordón para evitar que puedan asir de ella sus enemigos. La barba, así recogida, era un gesto belicoso, una especie de desafío que preocupa a los que miran al Cid en la corte (v. 3124-25, 3273-74)' — 'Plucking the beard was one of the gravest insults (p. 119, note), and the Cid, fearing an affront, gathers up his beard with a cord so that his enemies cannot lay hold of it. The beard, gathered up in this way, was a warlike gesture, a kind of challenge that troubles those who look at the Cid in the court (vv. 3124–25, 3273–74).' (Pidal prints 119 with a small subscript 19: page 119, line 19, and the note to it. That page is his prose reconstruction of the lost opening, where the Çid takes Count García Ordóñez prisoner at Cabra and plucks a tuft of his beard; the note there says that plucking a man's beard was a common affront that the laws punished with heavy fines. Checked on the scan, PDF p. 123.) por tal lo faze esto que, 'he does this for this reason, that' (lo … esto, the object said twice). recabdar, two readings: Pidal's note to v. 3098: 'recabdar puede tener aquí el sentido de "lograr, conseguir" (Bello, Obras, II, 285: "porque quería cobrar lo suyo"), o bien el de "prevenir, disponer" (D. Hinard: "parece qu'il veut garantir toute sa personne"; igual Adam y Bertoni)' — 'recabdar may here mean "to obtain, achieve" (Bello, Obras, II, 285: "because he wanted to recover what was his"), or else "to forestall, make provision" (D. Hinard: "for he wishes to safeguard his whole person"; so too Adam and Bertoni).' (parece in the French is so printed, for parce.) Pidal does not choose; our 'secure' is meant to hold both (to get back his own, to keep himself safe), and is uncertain. todo lo s[o], 'all that is his' (so = suyo, the o Pidal's).

sentences.t:
De suso cubrió un manto que es de grant valor,
en el[le] abrien que ve[er] quantos que i son.
sentences.l:
On top he-covered a mantle that is of great worth,
in it they-would-have what to-see as-many that there are.
sentences.i: Over all he put on a mantle of great price; all who were there would find something to gaze at in it.
sentences.n: De suso, 'above, on top'. Pidal's note to v. 3099: 'cubrió un manto, "vistió un manto", construcción usual hasta en el siglo XVII' — 'cubrió un manto, "he put on a mantle", a usual construction down to the seventeenth century'. de grant valor, 'of great worth' (grant = grande). en el[le], 'in it': elle is the old form of él, the le in Pidal's italic. abrien que ve[er], 'they would have something to see' (abrien = habrían, conditional of aver; aver que + infinitive, 'to have something to …'). veer = ver: on the scan the v and first e are roman and the e r italic, so ve[er], Pidal restoring the full old form (the extent of the italic was checked at high zoom and agrees with the pinned text). quantos que i son, 'as many as are there', que doubling quantos (as at v. 3037).

sentences.i: With the hundred he had ordered to make ready, he mounts in haste and rides out from San Servando; thus my Çid went, arrayed, to the court.
sentences.n: Pidal indents v. 3101, a fresh paragraph. Con aquestos çiento, 'with these hundred' (aquestos = estos). que adobar mandó, 'whom he ordered to make ready', mandar + infinitive. apriessa, 'quickly, in haste'. cavalga, 'he mounts, rides' (present), then salió, 'he went out' (preterite): tense-mixing. San Serván, 'San Servando' (house), the church where he kept his vigil (last part). iva = iba, 'was going'. mio Cid is printed here without the cedilla (Cid, not Çid), as the scan shows; kept, and 'my Çid' in the English as elsewhere. adobado, 'equipped, arrayed'. a lla cort, 'to the court' (lla = la, the l doubled after a, a spelling of the join between words, like ssu at v. 3062).

sentences.i: At the outer gate he dismounts at his ease; my Çid goes in with all his men, soberly: he walks in the middle, and the hundred all around him.
sentences.n: Pidal indents v. 3104, another paragraph. Ala = a la, run together as printed. puerta de fuera, 'the outer door, outer gate'. descavalga, 'he dismounts'. a sabor, 'at his pleasure, at ease'. cuerdamientra, 'wisely, prudently, soberly' (cuerdo, 'sensible'). Pidal's note to v. 3105: 'Los adverbios terminados en -mientra son raros, pero existe esta forma en vez de -miente' — 'Adverbs ending in -mientra are rare, but this form does exist instead of -miente' (modern -mente). con todos los sos, 'with all his own' (sos = suyos). el[le] = él, 'he', the le Pidal's (as at v. 3100). en medio, 'in the middle'. elos = e los, 'and the', run together as printed. aderredor = alrededor, 'around'. The colon at the end of v. 3105 is Pidal's.

sentences.t:
Quando lo vieron entrar al que en buen ora naçió.
levantós en pie el buen rey don Alfons
sentences.l:
When him they-saw enter him who in good hour was-born.
rose-himself on foot the good king don Alfons
sentences.i: When they saw him come in, he who was born in a good hour, the good King Alfonso rose to his feet,
sentences.n: Quando lo vieron entrar al que …, 'when they saw him enter, him who …': lo and al que name the same man twice. el que en buen ora naçió, the formula (house). Pidal prints a full stop after naçió and begins v. 3108 with small levantós, as printed: the sentence plainly runs on (the when-clause needs the next line), so the stop is kept but not read as an end; possibly a misprint for a comma. levantós = levantó + se, 'rose', the se cut to s and glued on. en pie, 'to his feet'. el buen rey don Alfons, 'the good King Alfonso' (Alfons, apocopated). The verse ends without punctuation, running on.

sentences.t:
e el co[m]de don Anrric e el co[m]de don Remont
e desí adelant, sabet, todos los otros [de la cort]:
a grant ondra lo reçiben al que en buen ora naçió.
sentences.l:
and the count don Anrric and the count don Remont
and from-there onward, know-ye, all the others [of the court]:
with great honour him they-receive him who in good hour was-born.
sentences.i: and Count Enrique and Count Remond, and after them — be sure of it — all the others of the court: with great honour they receive him who was born in a good hour.
sentences.n: co[m]de, 'count', the m Pidal's both times. don Anrric, 'Count Enrique' (house); don Remont, 'Count Remond' (house; spelt Remont here, Remond at v. 3002). desí adelant, 'from then on, after that' (desí = desde allí; adelant = adelante, apocopated). sabet = sabed, 'know, be sure', the narrator speaking to his hearers. todos los otros [de la cort], 'all the others of the court': de la cort is wholly in Pidal's italic, his restoration. a grant ondra, 'with great honour' (ondra = honra). lo reçiben al que …, the object said twice again.

sentences.t:
Nos quiso levantar el Crespo de Grañón,
nin todos los del bando de ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l:
Not-himself wanted to-rise the Curly-one of Grañón,
nor all those of-the party of infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: The Curly-haired of Grañón would not rise, nor any of the faction of the Infantes of Carrión.
sentences.n: Nos quiso levantar = non se quiso levantar, 'he would not rise' (Nos = non + se, house). el Crespo de Grañón, 'the Curly-haired of Grañón' (as in the last part, v. 3007; crespo, 'curly'). Pidal's note to v. 3112: 'El Crespo de Grañón, el conde García Ordóñez, p. 21-22' — 'The Crespo of Grañón, Count García Ordóñez, pp. 21–22' (of his introduction): the Count García of v. 2997 and the Garci Ordóñez of v. 1345, the Çid's old enemy. nin = ni, 'nor'. nin todos los del bando, 'nor all those of the faction', that is, none of them (bando, 'faction, party'). ifantes de Carrión, without the article.

sentences.t:
El rey [a mio] Çid: [a las manos le tomó]:
“Venid acá se[er] [comigo], Campeador,
sentences.l:
The king [to my] Çid: [by the hands him he-took]:
“Come here to-sit [with-me], Campeador,
sentences.i: The king took my Çid by the hands: “Come here and sit with me, Campeador,
sentences.n: Most of v. 3114 is Pidal's: a mio and the whole second half-line, a las manos le tomó, are in his italic, his restorations; only El rey … Çid is the manuscript's. The colon after Çid and the colon at the line's end are as printed; the sense is 'The king took my Çid by the hands' (tomar a uno a las manos, 'to take someone by the hands'; le, 'him'). Pidal indents v. 3114, a fresh paragraph. 3114b is Pidal's own number, printed in his margin. Venid acá, 'come here' (vos imperative, the king to the Çid in the respectful plural). se[er], 'to sit' (seer, the old verb from Latin sedere, 'sit'): the s and first e roman, the e r in Pidal's italic, checked on the scan at high zoom and agreeing with the pinned text. [comigo], 'with me', wholly Pidal's. Campeador, 'Campeador', the battle-champion.

sentences.t:
en aqueste escaño quem diestes vos en don;
maguer que âlgunos pesa, mejor sodes que nos.”
sentences.l:
on this bench that-to-me you-gave you as gift;
although that to-some it-grieves, better you-are than we.”
sentences.i: on this bench that you gave me as a gift; though it grieve some, you are better than we.”
sentences.n: aqueste escaño, 'this bench', a long seat of honour. quem = que me, 'that … me', the me cut to m and glued on. diestes = disteis, 'you gave' (vos form). en don, 'as a gift'. Pidal's note to v. 3115: 'Omite el juglar decirnos cuándo hizo el Cid este regalo, p. 85. Las Crónicas omiten la mención de este don del Cid' — 'The minstrel omits to tell us when the Cid made this gift, p. 85. The Chronicles leave out any mention of this gift of the Cid's.' maguer que, 'although'. âlgunos = a + algunos, 'to some', Pidal's circumflex marking two words run together (house, as ên, lâ): maguer que a algunos pesa, 'though it grieves some'. pesa, 'it weighs on, grieves', with the present indicative as printed. mejor sodes que nos, 'you are better than we' (sodes = sois; nos, 'we', the royal plural). Pidal's note to v. 3116: 'mejor sodes que nos parece excesivo en boca del rey, pero era frase usual de cortesía: el que más vale que nos, 1940; comp. por o valdremos más, 1521; más valemos por vos, 2517' — 'mejor sodes que nos seems excessive in the king's mouth, but it was a usual courtesy phrase: "he who is worth more than we", v. 1940; compare "whereby we shall be worth more", v. 1521; "we are worth more through you", v. 2517.'

sentences.i: Then he who won Valencia gave him many thanks: “Sit on your own bench, as king and lord; here I will sit, with all these men of mine.”
sentences.n: Essora = entonces, 'then'. dixo muchas merçedes, 'said many thanks' (merçed, 'mercy, favour', here 'thanks'). el que Valençia gañó, 'he who won Valencia' (gañó = ganó; Valençia kept in the literal line, 'Valencia' in the English, house). se[e]d, 'sit' (vos imperative of seer, = sed): the first e roman, the second in Pidal's italic, so the restored letter is the second e, as the pinned text has it. commo rey e señor, 'as king and lord'. acá posaré, 'here I shall sit, settle' (posar, 'to sit down, lodge'). aquestos mios, 'these men of mine'. The Çid declines the honour, the point Pidal's rubric marks: El Cid rehusa, 'the Cid declines'.

sentences.t: Lo que dixo el Çid al rey plogo de coraçón.
sentences.l: What said the Çid to-the king it-pleased from heart.
sentences.i: What the Çid said pleased the king with all his heart.
sentences.n: Lo que dixo el Çid, 'what the Çid said', the subject of plogo, 'it pleased' (old strong preterite of placer, = plugo). al rey, 'the king', the one pleased (placer takes a dative of the person pleased). de coraçón, 'from the heart, heartily'.

sentences.t:
En un escaño torniño essora mio Çid posó,
los çiento quel aguardan posan aderredor.
sentences.l:
On a bench turned then my Çid sat,
the hundred that-him guard sit around.
sentences.i: Then my Çid took his seat on a bench of turned wood, and the hundred who attend him sit all around.
sentences.n: En un escaño torniño, 'on a turned bench'. Pidal's note to v. 3121: 'escaño torniño, "torneado". Los Romances y las Crónicas suponen que este escaño lo ganó el Cid al rey Búcar o al rey Yúcef. Cervantes lo recuerda también como el asiento más honroso que podía imaginarse: "merecía el mismo escaño del Cid Ruidiaz Campeador" (Quijote, II, 33)' — 'escaño torniño, "turned" (on the lathe). The ballads and the Chronicles suppose that the Cid won this bench from King Búcar or King Yúsuf. Cervantes too remembers it as the most honourable seat imaginable: "he deserved the very bench of the Cid Ruy Díaz Campeador" (Don Quixote, II, 33).' essora, 'then'. posó, 'sat down' (posar). quel = que le, 'who … him', the le cut to l. aguardan, 'guard, attend, wait upon'. posan aderredor, 'sit around' (aderredor = alrededor). The preterite posó, then the present posan: tense-mixing.

sentences.i: All who are in the court are gazing at my Çid, at the beard he wore long and bound with the cord; in his array he looks a true man indeed.
sentences.n: Catando están, 'are looking, gazing' (catar, 'to look at'; estar + gerund, as now). quantos ha en la cort, 'as many as there are in the court' (ha = hay). a la barba que avié luenga e presa con el cordón, 'at the beard that he had long and fastened with the cord' (avié, 'he had'; presa, participle of prender, fem. with barba). Pidal's note to v. 3124: 'Compárese v. 3097' — 'Compare v. 3097' (the bound beard as a challenge: see the note there). aguisamientos, 'array, accoutrements' (aguisar, 'to equip'). bien semeja varón, 'he well looks a man' (semejar, 'to seem, look like'); varón, 'man', a man in full, a true man.

sentences.t: Nol pueden catar de vergüença ifantes de Carrión.
sentences.l: Not-him they-can look-at for shame infantes of Carrión.
sentences.i: For shame the Infantes of Carrión cannot look him in the face.
sentences.n: Nol = non le, 'not … him', the le cut to l and glued on. pueden catar, 'they can look at' (catar again, set against the whole court's gaze in v. 3123). de vergüença, 'for shame' (vergüença = vergüenza). ifantes de Carrión, without the article, the subject at the line's end. The part ends here; tirada 137 runs on, with the king rising to open the session (v. 3127), in the next part.
